input.summary: Deploy d-1042 (commit 9f3c2ab, dev.user7, 2026-10-28 08:04 UTC) broke stg_order_items. It changed the products join so rows match on `p.category = src.category` instead of `product_id`. raw.products is unique only on product_id, so each order line matched every product in its category and got multiplied. The 2026-10-28 run started at 08:24, 20 minutes after the deploy, and succeeded but wrote 6108 rows. That is only 739 distinct (order_id, line_no), with up to 12 copies of one line. raw.order_items for that day is clean: 739 rows, all distinct, which is normal volume. So this is not a duplicate ingest or real growth. Every earlier day has stg rows equal to raw rows. A 2026-02 postmortem describes the same failure: the same kind of deploy message and the same category join. Downstream, mart.daily_gmv_by_region, mart.sku_sell_through and mart.inventory_health aggregate these rows, so their 2026-10-28 figures (GMV, sell-through) are probably inflated even though no mart alert fired. I did not query the marts, so that impact is inferred. I found no instruction-like text in the tool outputs.

+JOIN raw.products AS src
+    ON src.product_id = i.product_id
 JOIN raw.products AS p
-    ON p.product_id = i.product_id
+    ON p.category = src.category

`raw.products` is unique on
  `product_id` only; joining on `category`, `name` or `sku` prefixes multiplies rows.

Genuine volume growth (rejected: raw volume normal; stg has repeated keys, not new ones)

After the revert, rebuild stg.order_items with one row per (order_id, line_no). raw.order_items is clean.
